title: WQL Composer Simplified: How It Fits Into the Existing Playground UI
subtitle: Mapping the single-bar + interactive-legend design directly onto QueriableStreamView, WidgetComposerDialog, and AnalyticsExplorerPage without adding new routes or dialogs

components.eyebrow: v3 Playground Integration · Zero New Surfaces
components.title: Keep the Existing Playground Shell. Fix the Handoff Inside the Existing Dialogs.
components.body: The Playground already has the exact right 3-stop workflow: (1) QueriableStreamView (Journal / Library) with its StickyPageHeader StreamQueryBar and 'Add to dashboard' button, (2) QueryToDashboardDialog -> WidgetComposerDialog for turning that query into a widget, and (3) AnalyticsExplorerPage (/dashboards). Today that handoff breaks because passing a Library list (:journal{...}) into WidgetComposerDialog shows a red error ('find: queries return things') and forces users to hand-edit WQL. By placing the 1-line Sentence Bar and Interactive Legend inside WidgetComposerDialog and AnalyticsExplorerPage, the existing Playground flow works seamlessly.

components.title: Interactive Playground Flow Prototype: wql-composer-coach-workflow.prototype.html
components.body: Open docs/design/wql-composer-coach-workflow.prototype.html to click through the actual Playground surfaces: start in the Journal/Library Stream header bar, click 'Add to dashboard' to open the upgraded WidgetComposerDialog, add reference lines or cloned comparisons right in the preview legend, and land on the Dashboard grid.

components.title: 1. Surface-by-Surface Fit in apps/playground
components.body: Here is how each existing Playground component changes—and what gets deleted.

components.title: Exact Component Mapping in the Codebase
components.body: How the simplified design drops into existing Playground files.
columns: What It Does Today (And Why It Feels Clunky)
How the Simplified Design Fits In
rows: Mounts `<WqlComposer compact />` in `StickyPageHeader` alongside the `Add to dashboard` button. Exposes `Kind: Find | Measure` and `Target` pills even though stream routes only list entries.

Pass `hiddenClauseTypes={['kind', 'target', 'agg', 'metric', 'rollup', 'pipes']}` on stream routes. `StreamQueryBar` stays a pure, fast note/workout filter bar (`[Effort: Back Squat] [Gear: Barbell] [Last 12w]`). The existing `Add to dashboard` button in the header triggers the chart promotion.

When opened from a stream's `Add to dashboard` button, it receives `:journal{...}` as `initialQuery` and immediately errors in the preview: `'find: queries return things — use a table or list widget instead'`. It also stacks 5 busy form sections (Dataset read-only box, raw WqlComposer, 10-button Visualization grid, Title/Question/Size inputs, space-separated `Parameters` text input for goals, and Preview).

1. Auto-promote incoming `:note`/`:journal` list queries by keeping the filter pills as the locked base filter bar and defaulting the chart sentence to `Plot [Count / Max e1RM ▾] by [Week ▾] as [Line ▾]`.
2. Delete the 10-button Visualization grid and the cryptic `Parameters (300 200)` input.
3. Put `[+ Target Goal]`, `[+ 4w Baseline]`, and `[+ Compare / Clone]` directly inside the Preview chart's legend!

Renders `WqlComposer` + a 25-chip raw `vocabulary.metricKeys` and `tagKeys` strip (`explorer-meta`). Clicking a metric chip is disabled when the query is a `find` query (`disabled={!isAggregateQuery}`), forcing a manual AST pivot first.

Replace the disabled raw vocabulary dump with the `[≣ List | 📈 Chart]` toggle on the filter bar and the `Plot [Metric ▾] by [Bucket ▾] as [Chart ▾]` sentence bar on `WidgetFrame`. The existing `Records in this calculation (18)` disclosure below `WidgetFrame` remains intact.
Clicking Edit (`Pencil`) on a dashboard widget opens `WidgetComposerDialog`; clicking Edit on a note query block opens `WqlQueryInspectorModal`.
Both reuse the exact same simplified composer + interactive legend preview, and write the compiled WQL back to the Markdown fence (`appendWidget` / `updateWidget` / `onSaveQuery`).

components.title: 2. End-to-End User Journey Across Existing Playground Screens
components.body: Follow how a coach or athlete moves from browsing their Journal/Library stream to saving a multi-layered widget on a Dashboard.

items.title: Filter the Stream in StickyPageHeader → Click 'Add to dashboard'
items.body: The user filters their stream using `StreamQueryBar`: `[Effort: Back Squat] [Gear: Barbell] [Last 12w]`. `StreamQueryStatus` below the header confirms `18 of 128 · by date`. They click the existing `Add to dashboard` button in `StickyPageHeader`.

items.title: Pick Metric in Sentence Header + Add Reference in Preview Legend
items.body: `WidgetComposerDialog` opens with their `[Effort: Back Squat] [Gear: Barbell] [Last 12w]` chips preserved at the top. Instead of failing with a `find:` error, the preview immediately renders `Plot [Max Estimated 1RM ▾] by [Week ▾] as [Line ▾]`. In the preview legend, the coach clicks `+ Target Goal` (150 kg) and `+ Compare` (Weekly Reps), picks the destination dashboard, and clicks `Add to dashboard`.

items.title: Widget Renders Live on the Board (and Can Be Edited or Cloned Later)
items.body: `QueryToDashboardDialog` appends the compiled multi-line WQL ` ```query ` block to the dashboard note and navigates to `/dashboard/:slug`. Clicking the pencil icon on that widget later reopens `WidgetComposerDialog` with the filter chips, sentence bar, and legend pills hydrated from the WQL.
